title: Affine smallness of perfect isomorphism classes
statement: Let $Y$ be an affine scheme in universe $u$ [def-pc-scheme], with derived categories for its module sheaves and module sheaves on its open sites [def-pc-derived-category]. The skeleton of the full subcategory of perfect objects [def-pc-perfect-complex] of $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ is $u$-small: its type of objects, equivalently perfect derived isomorphism classes, is equivalent to a type in universe $u$. No quasi-separatedness hypothesis beyond affineness and no relation between the morphism universe $w$ and $u$ is imposed.

source.place: Lemma perfect-lemma-perfect-affine, Tag 08EB; the finite-projective encoding in Step 1 of lem-pc-perfect-complexes-compact-set

proof.text: Use exists_affine_finite_module_presentation with the explicit affineModuleComplexFunctor: every perfect quasi-coherent object is isomorphic in the ambient derived category to the image of a complex with finite terms.

Define FiniteTermModel A by integer-indexed FGModuleRepr A terms, module-category differentials, and the shape and square-zero identities. This structure is in Type u. Given a finite-term complex P, Mathlib FGModuleRepr.ofFinite and ofFiniteEquiv give representatives X_n and isomorphisms e_n : X_n ≅ P_n. Define d_ij = e_i.hom ≫ P.d i j ≫ e_j.inv. Cancellation proves the shape and square-zero conditions and HomologicalComplex.Hom.isoOfComponents gives an isomorphism M.complex ≅ P. No boundedness or projectivity is needed for this larger small family.

Let f send a finite-term model to the skeleton class of its associated derived sheaf. The range of f is u-small. The composite of the perfect and quasi-coherent full-subcategory inclusions is fully faithful, so its map on skeletons is injective. The presentation theorem and the preceding complex isomorphism put every perfect skeleton class in the range of f. Restrict this injective map to Set.range f and apply small_of_injective.
